findings.title: Protected-global carve-out is suppressible by a forged successor row in the canonical registry
findings.detail: _declared_terminal_anchors reads plans/CYCLE_REGISTRY.json from the WORKING TREE at repo_root and accepts any row with head_semantics=TERMINAL_ANCHOR and a well-formed sha. A7 reproduced: an (uncommitted or committed) forged row whose terminal_anchor_sha is >= the tamper commit makes a post-anchor HYPOTHESIS_LEDGER.md edit informational for EVERY row (0 findings), because _successor_covered sees the touch as ancestor-covered. Reaching this state requires deliberately fabricating an audited-anchor declaration - i.e. forging the canonical registry that the whole CAS+journal/gate/A7 apparatus exists to authorize; a forger with that power can already re-anchor any row directly. Uncovered, malformed, unreadable-registry and non-ancestor cases all still fire HIGH (proven). The delta did relax the pre-fix unconditional ledger HIGH, but only along the successor-anchor seam that plan 12.2 itself defines.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: resolve successor anchors from a pinned COMMITTED registry revision (e.g. the blob at the live tip rather than the working tree) and/or require the covering anchor to be reachable from the branch tip; log any registry row whose terminal_anchor_sha is NOT an ancestor of the live tip as a visible anomaly.
